study_identification_part.si_4_title: Replicating extensive brain structural heterogeneity in individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study; discovery sample and two replication samples selected from the TOP database.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study... The two replication samples were selected from the TOP-database

answer.TOP: Discovery sample (normative modeling and group comparisons) and replication samples 1 and 2 (replication of normative modeling and group comparisons)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy individuals from TOP used to estimate the normative model; the model applied to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder patients in discovery and replication samples.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: For replication sample 1, we included ... 400 healthy individuals. As the replication sample 2, we included 312 healthy individuals... As the discovery sample, we selected 256 healthy individuals... we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, and then applied one model across all healthy individuals to patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
